newsitem.title: INDIA: India call ends up, gilt yields rise in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: India call ends up, gilt yields rise in dull trade.

text.p: Indian call money ended in the 6.0-6.25 percent range on Wednesday, up from the day's opening of 5.75-6.0 percent, dealers said.
Deals were struck at rates up to 6.50 percent during the day, they said.
"There seems to be no reason for the hardening in call rates today," a dealer at a foreign bank said. "Lenders seem to be pushing up rates."

Dealers said they expected call rates to move up next week as banks feel the impact of an outflow of funds on account of advance tax payments by corporates and subscription to a 20 billion-rupee auction of six-year government securities on September 17.
Corporates have to make advance tax payments, estimated at 60 billion rupees, before September 15.
"These two factors should result in a firming up of call rates," a dealer said.

Dealers reported a stray seven-day ready-forward (repo) transaction at 7.5 percent. Most of the quotes for 14-day repos were quoted between 10.0 percent and 11.0 percent, they said. "This is an indication that call money rates are expected to be be around 10 percent," a dealer said.

Dealers said yields on government securities moved up in dull trade on Wednesday. The 13.50 percent 1997 government of India stock was traded at a yield of 13.16 percent against Tuesday's 13.06 percent.
The yield on the treasury bill maturing on September 30 moved up from 7.5 percent to 9.0 percent, a dealer said.
Dealers said a certificate of deposit maturing on January 24, 1997 was traded in the secondary market at a yield of 13.75 percent.
Three-month commercial paper was quoted at 14 percent for top-rated corporates in the primary market, dealers said.
The rates on intercorporate deposits remained steady in the 17.0-19.0 percent range for top-rated borrowers, dealers said.
